about: Nodes of the meteorology lineage graph, type "observing-system": what measures the atmosphere. Ids are stable (incident.entities@ may adopt them); meaning is in the edges (meteorology/edges/), not here.

nodes.name: Surface weather stations (SYNOP)
nodes.summary: Staffed and automatic stations on land reporting pressure, wind, temperature, humidity and rain at fixed hours; exchanged between countries through the WMO Global Observing System.

nodes.name: IPMA's surface stations
nodes.summary: Portugal's network of automatic stations; hourly observations are in IPMA's open data (the feed our data room reads for Lisbon and Madeira).

nodes.name: Airport observations (METAR)
nodes.summary: Routine aerodrome reports for aviation: wind with gusts, visibility, cloud, pressure. Lisbon airport (LPPT) is the only gust series our data room holds.

nodes.name: Radiosondes (weather balloons)
nodes.summary: Balloon-borne instruments giving a vertical profile of temperature, humidity and wind, usually twice a day (00 and 12 UTC).

nodes.name: Aircraft reports (AMDAR)
nodes.summary: Automated wind and temperature reports from commercial aircraft during climb, cruise and descent.

nodes.name: Buoys and ships
nodes.summary: Drifting and moored buoys and voluntary observing ships: pressure, wind, waves and sea temperature over the ocean, where a storm like Charles forms.

nodes.name: IPMA's weather radars
nodes.summary: Portugal's Doppler radars (mainland and islands): rain intensity every few minutes.

nodes.name: OPERA (the European radar composite)
nodes.summary: EUMETNET's programme that exchanges and composites the national weather radars of its members.

nodes.name: Meteosat (geostationary)
nodes.summary: EUMETSAT's geostationary satellites over Europe, Africa and the Atlantic: an image of the whole disc every few minutes (second and third generation).

nodes.name: Metop (polar orbiters)
nodes.summary: EUMETSAT's polar-orbiting satellites: soundings of temperature and humidity and scatterometer winds over the sea, the largest single satellite contribution to forecast skill in many studies.

nodes.name: JPSS and NOAA polar orbiters
nodes.summary: The United States' polar-orbiting weather satellites (NOAA-20, NOAA-21, Suomi NPP).

nodes.name: GOES (geostationary, Americas)
nodes.summary: NOAA's geostationary satellites over the Americas and the western Atlantic; GOES-East sees the mid-Atlantic where storms bound for Iberia deepen.

nodes.name: Blitzortung (community lightning network)
nodes.summary: A volunteer network of lightning receivers; data is for the contributing station owners.

nodes.name: Personal weather stations (Weather Underground network)
nodes.summary: Home weather stations whose owners upload to Weather Underground: dense in cities, of uneven quality, not part of the official exchange.

nodes.name: Instituto Hidrográfico's wave buoys
nodes.summary: Moored buoys off the Portuguese coast measuring wave height, period and direction: what a rough-sea warning is checked against.
